_strings.@@02a5b675ad39: Minnesota Child and Dependent Care Credit — MN taxpayers who paid someone (other than a dependent child or stepchild younger than 19) to care for a qualifying person while you (and your spouse if filing jointly) were working or looking for work — qualifying person and expenses are the same as for the federal child and dependent care credit. Also available to licensed family daycare operators caring for their own dependent child under age six, and for a child born in 2024 if you did not participate in a pre-tax dependent care assistance program. Refundable, unlike the federal credit.

_strings.@@270ce383619f: Law change NOT modeled by the engine (status final_form_published): HEADLINE 2024 CHANGE — the RENTER'S CREDIT moved ONTO the income tax return. Beginning with rent paid in tax year 2024, renters claim the credit on the NEW Schedule M1RENT filed WITH Form M1 (flowing to Schedule M1REF, then Form M1 line 22): "Renter's Credit ... complete Schedule M1RENT ... Renters should not complete Form M1PR", which now remains only for homeowners' Homestead Credit Refund. For tax year 2023 the same relief was claimed on the separate Form M1PR return (renter's property tax refund). CRP information must be provided with the return; for 2024 the maximum credit is $2,640 and household income must be less than $75,390. _strings.@@37f1b0c2a351: Treaty conformity — MN conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from MN income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the MN return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Minnesota's resident return (Form M1) starts from federal adjusted gross income: the 2024 M1 instructions for Line 1 state "Line 1—Federal Adjusted Gross Income. Enter your 2024 federal adjusted gross income from line 11 of Form 1040 or 1040-SR, or 1040-NR." Federally treaty-exempt income is already excluded from federal AGI and therefore flows through. The Minnesota additions (M1 line 2 = Schedule M1M line 10 and Schedule M1MB line 9) contain NO line that adds back income exempt under a U.S. income tax treaty. The only treaty references in the 2024 M1 instructions are FAVORABLE to the taxpayer (a nonresident alien may claim the standard deduction if allowed by a U.S. income tax treaty — repeated in the What's New standard-deduction section and the Line 4 Standard Deduction Table note). Because there is no treaty addback, treaty-exempt income is not re-taxed -> conforms.
_strings.@@4a8c431fe22b: Law change NOT modeled by the engine (status final_form_published): NEW for 2024 filings — a taxpayer may ELECT ADVANCE PAYMENTS of their 2025 Child Tax Credit on Schedule M1CWFC; electing also makes them eligible for a 2025 Minimum Credit of up to 50% of the prior-year credit, and paper filers who elect mail the return to Mail Station 0015 instead of Mail Station 0010. The credit itself stays at $1,750 per qualifying child under age 18 with no cap on the number of qualifying children. Resolve via: 2024 Schedule M1CWFC and its instructions (the citation URL) — the election, the advance payment amounts and the 2025 Minimum Credit are administered by the MN DOR, not computed here.

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: Form M1 line 10: "Tax from the table or schedules in the Form M1 instructions". Instructions, Line 10 — Tax From Table: "Using the amount on line 9, find the tax amount in the column under your filing status." Tax Rate Schedules, p.37: "You must use these schedules if line 9 of Form M1 is $90,000 or more... If line 9 of Form M1 is less than $90,000, you must use the tax table on pages 30 through 36." This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Base guidance: Supply Form M1 line 1 = federal adjusted gross income (federal Form 1040/1040-SR/1040-NR line 11), adjusted for Minnesota items if any apply: ADD M1 line 2 additions (Schedule M1M line 10 and Schedule M1MB line 9) and SUBTRACT M1 line 6 (state income tax refund from federal Schedule 1 line 1) and M1 line 7 subtractions (Schedule M1M line 35 and Schedule M1MB line 21). The op then subtracts the shipped per-status standard deduction (M1 line 4) and $5,050 per dependent (M1 line 5) to reach M1 line 9, Minnesota taxable income, to which the rate schedule applies. Pass exemptions_count = 0 (Minnesota has no taxpayer/spouse personal exemption) and dependents_count = number of dependents claimed on Schedule M1DQC. Adjudication note (two-pass): the 2024 schedules were drafted from the M1 booklet's p.37 Tax Rate Schedules and re-verified digit-by-digit against the DOR's Dec 12, 2023 indexing press release AND the Tax Year 2024 Tax Professional Desk Reference Chart — all three agree on every boundary (single 31,690/104,090/193,240; MFJ 46,330/184,040/321,450; MFS 23,165/92,020/160,725 — exactly half of MFJ; HoH 39,010/156,760/256,880), the four rates (5.35%/6.80%/7.85%/9.85%, unchanged from 2023), the standard deduction ($14,575/$29,150/$14,575/$21,900), and the $5,050 dependent exemption. 2024 indexing factor: +5.376%, rounded to the nearest $10. TAX TABLE MANDATE below $90,000: 'If line 9 of Form M1 is less than $90,000, you must use the tax table on pages 30 through 36' (2024 M1 instructions, p.37); the rate schedules are only for line 9 of $90,000 or more. The table is built on $100-band midpoints chained from the printed schedule constants, so bracket math may differ by a few dollars within table bands — the filed form must use the table. (Spot-checked: table row $83,300-$83,400 prints 5,208 / 4,996 / 5,332 / 5,102 for Single/MFJ/MFS/HoH — all four equal midpoint bracket math at $83,350.) Qualifying Surviving Spouse: the p.37 rate-schedule column is titled 'Married filing jointly or qualifying widow(er)' — QSS uses the MFJ schedule exactly as mapped here, and the QSS standard deduction ($29,150 with 0 age/blind boxes) equals MFJ. Minnesota has NO personal exemption for the taxpayer or spouse: Form M1 line 5 is for DEPENDENTS only ($5,050 per dependent from Schedule M1DQC). Callers must pass exemptions_count = 0 and put dependents in dependents_count. Dependent-exemption phase-out NOT modeled (Worksheet for Line 5): the $5,050-per-dependent total is reduced by 2% for each $2,500 ($1,250 MFS) that M1 line 1 AGI exceeds $232,550 Single / $290,700 Head of Household / $348,850 MFJ-or-Surviving-Spouse / $174,425 MFS, and is $0 once the excess is more than $122,500 ($61,250 MFS). Standard-deduction limitation NOT modeled (Worksheets A & B for Line 4): if M1 line 1 AGI exceeds $232,500 ($116,250 MFS), the deduction is reduced by the LESSER of 80% of the deduction or [3% of the excess over $232,500/$116,250 (capped: enter $88,850, or $44,425 MFS, if AGI exceeds $321,350/$160,675) + 10% of the excess over $321,350 ($160,675 MFS)]; if AGI exceeds $1,053,750, the deduction is reduced by 80% (Worksheet B). Additional standard deduction for age 65+/blind NOT modeled (Standard Deduction Table for Line 4): +$1,950 per checked box for Single and Head of Household (up to 2 boxes); +$1,550 per checked box for Married Filing Jointly (up to 4), Married Filing Separately (up to 4), and Qualified Surviving Spouse (up to 2). Born before January 2, 1960 counts as 65 or older. Enter it on the form's line 4. Standard-deduction gates NOT modeled: Married Filing Separately gets NO standard deduction if the spouse claims itemized deductions ('Not allowed' row); nonresident aliens may claim it only if allowed by a U.S. income tax treaty; a filer claimable as another's dependent uses the Worksheet for Line 4 - Dependent Standard Deduction (greater of $1,300 or earned income + $400, capped at $14,575, plus $1,950/$1,550 age/blind additions) — itemizers use Schedule M1SA instead. Printed rate-schedule constants check: every '$X +' constant equals the exact cumulative sum of the prior brackets rounded to the cent (single 1,695.42/6,618.62 vs exact 1,695.415/6,618.615; MFJ 2,478.66/11,842.94 vs exact 2,478.655/11,842.935; MFS 1,239.33/5,921.47 vs exact 1,239.3275/5,921.4675; HoH 2,087.04/10,094.04 vs exact 2,087.035/10,094.035), EXCEPT the top-bracket constants, which chain the rounded prior constant: single $13,616.90 vs $13,616.89 exact, MFJ $22,629.63 vs $22,629.62, HoH $17,953.46 vs $17,953.455 (MFS $11,314.81 is exact). Maximum divergence from pure marginal math: $0.01. NOT modeled — amounts added after line 10: Minnesota Alternative Minimum Tax (Schedule M1MT, M1 line 11; can apply even without federal AMT) and M1 line 14 other taxes: Schedule M1HOME first-time-homebuyer recapture, Schedule M1529 education-savings-account recapture, Schedule M1LS tax on lump-sum distributions, and — NEW for 2024 — the Net Investment Income Tax (Schedule NIIT) on individuals with net investment income greater than $1,000,000. Part-year residents and nonresidents: tax is prorated by the Minnesota-source percentage on Schedule M1NR (M1 lines 13/13a/13b) — NOT modeled; this pack computes full-year-resident tax. M1 line 9 (Minnesota taxable income) = line 3 (federal AGI + line 2 additions) - line 4 (standard/itemized deduction) - line 5 (dependent exemptions) - line 6 (taxable state income tax refund) - line 7 (M1M/M1MB subtractions). If additions, subtractions, or a taxable state refund apply, adjust the supplied taxable_base per base_guidance. The form says 'If zero or less, leave blank' — the engine's max(0, ...) floor matches. Rounding: the M1 instructions say 'Round the dollar amounts to the nearest dollar. For example: 129.49 becomes 129, and 129.50 becomes 130' (Getting Started) — the engine's round-half-up to whole dollars matches.
